ell_definition: E[H1(S(1) intersect A)]=ell*area(A), where S(1) is all routes between independent unit-intensity whole-plane Poisson sample endpoints, not the continuum all-point network, MST, minimal Steiner network, or finite-point intensity.
axioms: Measurable consistent finite-dimensional laws of finite, nonselfintersecting rectifiable polygonal/jagged routes with reversal symmetry.
Compatibility: any two routes meeting twice share the subroute between those meeting points.
Invariance in law under all planar translations, rotations and positive Euclidean scalings.
Independent Poisson sampling and iid binomial endpoints are independent of the common random route process, not mutually independent routes.
Delta=E length R(0,(1,0)) finite, ell finite, and p(1) finite for a full SIRSN; weak SIRSN only assumes ell.
No axiom requires Euclidean-shortest routes, convex-hull containment, bounded geometric wandering, ergodicity, higher route moments or uniform integrability of distant total length.
conventions: Length is Euclidean one-dimensional union length; shared overlapping edges counted once, not traffic weight, travel time, or sum of pair lengths.
With0 or1 sample endpoints the pair-route union has length0.
Poisson process restricted to a square of area a has N~Poisson(lambda*a); conditional on N=n endpoints are iid uniform in that square independently of the route field.
S_Q(lambda) means union for Poisson endpoints inside Q; S(lambda) uses all whole-plane endpoints. Whole length and clipped length in Q are distinct.
Scaling c sends S(lambda) in law to S(lambda/c^2), and ell(lambda)=sqrt(lambda)*ell.
All expectations include independent endpoint sampling and route-field randomness; all limits are annealed unless an additional mode is proved.
